\caption{Every optimization, put back one at a time. Rung \emph{pre-optimization} runs one instrumented build with every ablatable change switched off (\texttt{SHMAP\_ABLATE}); each rung to its right switches exactly one more back on, in the layer order this note argues. Adjacent rungs therefore differ by one change and nothing else --- same binary, machine, compiler and input --- so a step is that change's worth \emph{given the ones before it}, which is the only sense in which these interacting changes have individual values. The two series are the two thread counts; the gap between them is row~4, threaded read mapping, which is a capability rather than a branch and so cannot be a rung. Row~8 is type- and build-level and is not ablated at all. Left: wall clock, bars at the median over 9 runs of the whole ladder and whiskers at min--max, so a step this host has not resolved is visible as one. The two parallelism rungs cannot move the one-worker series at all --- at \texttt{-@1} both take the serial path in either position --- so their flat steps there are structure, not noise. Right: peak resident set --- one worker's genome-sized accumulator hides under the index-build peak, but \texttt{-@8} workers' copies do not, which is the scaling argument in one picture. Every rung's mapping is byte-identical; the run fails otherwise. Numbers, per-stage timers and the spread behind every bar in \texttt{figure\_ablation.tsv}.}
\label{fig:ablation}
